review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines BNRankGe (the discrete Brill–Noether rank predicate), its reformulation bnRankGe_iff_contained, and the numerical invariant bnRank. bnRank is built from Mathlib's sSup on ℤ, with Int.csSup_mem and le_csSup in the proofs. The file also has monotonicity and degree-ceiling lemmas and a transport lemma along LaplacianEquiv. All of these are specific to chip-firing graphs and Lim–Payne–Potashnik. Mathlib has no Brill–Noether rank, no divisor rank on graphs, and no winnable or effective predicates for graph divisors, so I found no competing version of an existing Mathlib, Batteries or core concept. The repeated `n • oneChip v` constructions are local proof devices, not a separate concept. bnRank is a named wrapper over sSup, which the rubric does not count as a defect. I did not search the Mathlib tree exhaustively. The conclusion rests on there being no Mathlib notion of chip-firing divisor rank or Brill–Noether rank. The related-library declarations (CFDiv, rank, winnable) are not Mathlib and are outside this rubric's scope.
